examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{店|みせ}を{開|ひら}く。
{地図|ちず}を{開|ひら}いて{道|みち}を{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I opened the map and checked the route.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{去年|きょねん}、{駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しいレストランを{開|ひら}いた。
examples.english: He opened a new restaurant in front of the station last year.

examples.japanese: パーティーを{開|ひら}く。
{来月|らいげつ}、{展覧会|てんらんかい}を{開|ひら}く{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: We plan to hold an exhibition next month.

examples.japanese: {講演会|こうえんかい}を{開|ひら}いて、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{集|あつ}まった。
examples.english: We held a lecture and many people gathered.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}の{誕生日|たんじょうび}に、サプライズパーティーを{開|ひら}いた。
examples.english: I threw a surprise party for my friend's birthday.

notes:
{開|ひら}く has two main meanings: (1) to open something physical, and (2) to hold/organize an event.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Takes を particle

DON'T CONFUSE (all use {開|ひら/あ}):
- {開|ひら}く: to open (formal), to hold events
- {開|あ}く: to open by itself (intransitive)
- {開|あ}ける: to open something (transitive, everyday)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {本|ほん}を{開|ひら}く: to open a book
- {会議|かいぎ}を{開|ひら}く: to hold a meeting
- パーティーを{開|ひら}く: to throw a party
- {店|みせ}を{開|ひら}く: to open a shop/business
- {目|め}を{開|ひら}く: to open one's eyes (literary)

REGISTER:
{開|ひら}く sounds more formal/literary than {開|あ}ける for physical opening. For events, {開|ひら}く is the standard choice.
